title: A finite coloring is a Roelcke coloring exactly when it depends only on the pattern with one finite substructure

standard_prerequisites.name: Roelcke colorings and joint embedding patterns
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a Fraisse structure the article attaches to each finite substructure and each joint embedding of a finite substructure into the structure the pattern of a copy, and a finite coloring of the copies is a Roelcke coloring when it is uniformly continuous for the Roelcke uniformity of the automorphism group, which the article shows is the same as depending only on those patterns. The author's own definitions and the surrounding results are the ones used by the counted statement and proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proposition is the combinatorial description of a single Roelcke coloring, and the article uses it to pass between a coloring of copies and a coloring of the patterns of one joint embedding.

core_obligations: Forward direction: assume that the coloring of the copies belongs to the Roelcke colorings of the automorphism group, fix the finite substructure and read the coloring as a coloring of the joint embedding patterns of that substructure, which the article's earlier work on the Roelcke uniformity supplies (source line 524).

Exhibit the finite substructure of the statement: take the substructure of the structure whose patterns exhaust the values the coloring takes, and observe that the coloring depends only on the pattern with that substructure, which is what the statement asks for (source line 524).

Converse direction: assume the coloring depends only on the pattern with one finite substructure, and show that it is uniformly continuous for the Roelcke uniformity, since the pattern map is continuous for the uniformity and the coloring factors through it (source line 524).

Combine: the two implications are the two directions of the equivalence, and the proof of the next statement of the article continues from the same block by lifting a finite set of such colorings to one coloring of the patterns of a larger substructure (source line 524).

proof_roadmap.step: Assume the coloring is Roelcke and fix the finite substructure; the coloring is then a coloring of the joint embedding patterns of that substructure.
Take the finite substructure whose patterns carry all the values of the coloring, which exhibits the dependence asked for in the statement.

Conversely, if the coloring depends only on the pattern with one finite substructure then it factors through the pattern map, which is continuous for the Roelcke uniformity, so the coloring is Roelcke.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 doi:10.5802/ahl.16 的 Proposition prop:Roelcke coloring（源 515-517 行，与相邻的 prop:RoelckeRP 共用证明块 523-525 行）：设 F 是 Fraïssé 结构、A∈Age(F)、χ 是有限着色，则 χ∈ROB(Aut(F)) 当且仅当存在有限子结构 Z 使 χ(a) 只依赖 [a,z]（z 取恒等嵌入）。证明要点不是例行核验：正方向要把「Roelcke 一致连续」翻成「只依赖模式」（用 F 的 Roelcke 一致同构与模式的关系，取出使取值穷尽的有限 Z）；反方向要把「只依赖 [a,z]」翻回一致连续（着色经**模式映射**分解，而模式映射对该一致结构连续）。难点在把一致结构语言与模式语言来回翻译，且 Z 的取法要显式给出。原文位置在证明的 524 行；同一块末句起就是相邻命题（量化形式）的证明，本卡不取那部分。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Proposition prop:Roelcke coloring at source lines 515-517 together with its proof at source lines 523-525. That proof environment is shared with the statement that follows it, prop:RoelckeRP at lines 519-521; the block proves the counted statement first and then continues with the neighbour, and the neighbour is declared as a navigation pointer. This is the pairing the gate reported as clean, and the two statements are not interderivable: one describes a single coloring, the other an equivalence quantified over all finite substructures, embeddings and colorings of patterns. The source is the publisher version of the article in Annales Henri Lebesgue 2 (2019), pages 149-185, DOI 10.5802/ahl.16, released under CC BY 4.0.

One earlier note of this lane called this statement uncountable on the ground that it has no proof of its own. That reading was wrong for this statement: the block at lines 523-525 does carry its argument, and the article prints the two statements as separate propositions because it uses each on its own. The recorded pairing makes the sharing explicit, and the neighbour is left as a pointer.
